latest.baseText: Medvedev beat Tiafoe for the 7th time in 9 meetings, 6-3, 6-4 in the group stage.

commentary.text: Medvedev started poorly and was the first to come under pressure but he saved a couple of break points and then won the first set 6-3. His defence was the strongest part of his game and he chased down ball after ball. Tiafoe made a perfect start to the second set with aggressive play and a crucial hold and he showed fine touch with his hands near the net. Medvedev stayed too solid and used his experience to win. He reached another semifinal at the season-ending championships in Turin, which he won in London in 2020 and his semifinal is on Saturday night.

blocks.label: after his win over Cobolli
blocks.text: I'm proud about the level that I'm playing today and the way that I'm feeling. The way that I felt on the court today was incredible. I'm just really happy that I'm getting more confident the way that I'm hitting the ball, the way that I'm seeing what's going on in the match and after that trying to find solutions. I'm getting more confident after every match.

blocks.label: on playing aggressively despite his thigh problem
blocks.text: Today's match, for me, was an important match because we were testing myself. I just felt great on court today. I try not to move that much, I try to be aggressive, to dominate the match as much as I can … I could do it. I tried to play as aggressive as I can, hitting the ball as hard as I could, trying not to move that much. So I'm just happy about it. I'm looking forward to tomorrow.

blocks.label: on recovering in time for the semi-final
blocks.text: The challenge now is not on the court, it's off the court, to do whatever it takes to be in a good shape, to feel physically ready for a battle tomorrow. It's going to be a really important half a day that I have ahead of me with my team, with my physio, with the doctor. Recovering is the most important thing now, we'll see how I feel tomorrow.

blocks.label: on managing the injury scare before this match
blocks.text: Yesterday was a really important day for me, to be honest. Obviously I felt something in the last match. Yesterday with the test, we decided not to practice, to rest. We went to have a walk, chill. And getting treatment morning, afternoon with my physio, this morning once again, really careful. Doing, I'm going to say, as best as we can do the things off the court to be ready and to be in a good shape for this match. I'm trying to learn from these moments. I'm trying to know myself a little bit better. I think these kinds of moments help you a lot to know yourself much better.

blocks.label: on speculation about his physical problem
blocks.text: I've seen so many things, that I'm going to retire, that I'm not going to play. Well, I'll leave it to you to choose the diagnosis that I really have after today's game.

blocks.label: on supporting his friend Flavio Cobolli
blocks.text: I'm here, whatever he needs, to talk, whatever it is, I'm here for him, because he's a great friend. We're going to see more about Flavio Cobolli in the future. I'm going to say that, because I'm sure about it.

Alcaraz is still unbeaten in his group after beating Cobolli 6–4, 6–1 in 65 minutes. It was Cobolli's first appearance at this event and he played it at home.

Alcaraz broke in the opening game. Cobolli saved two set points with Alcaraz 5–3 up but Alcaraz served out the set to lead by a set. From there the match turned completely: he broke three times in the second set, the last one for the match. Alcaraz knows how good it was: "I just felt great on court today."

It showed in how he played. He hit his forehand hard and found a winning backhand up the line. Alcaraz was at his best when it mattered most, never facing a break point and winning 84% of his first-serve points, far above his 74% average on hard.

Alcaraz called the physio in his previous group match here and did not call for one in this match.

A deserved win for Alcaraz: a clean, dominant performance, with a dominance ratio of 1.97 and just 14 unforced errors. Shelton waits in his next match.

blocks.label: after his win over Fils
blocks.text: I thought the first two matches were very, very high level. Today I thought I played a little bit worse from the baseline, but I'm very happy to have won all three matches against three very difficult opponents. I'm happy to be through in straight sets.

blocks.label: on his recurring ankle pain against Fils
blocks.text: Unfortunately, I started feeling my ankle again. I'll probably feel my ankle sometimes until the end of my career. It's unfortunately the injury that I had, it's quite big. The ankle unfortunately is a topic for me that probably will stay until the end of my career with the injury I had four years ago. Every once in a while, it happens like that. There is no particular reason why it happens. There is nothing like a single movement that makes it go. I know what it is. It's nothing out of the ordinary. Look, I'm going to do everything I can to be pain-free on Saturday, but this is something that I have to live with nowadays. I hope I'll be 100 percent on Saturday.

blocks.label: on how the ankle affects his serve
blocks.text: On the serve more than on the baseline, because I feel like I can still move well. But you can see immediately my serve speed goes down, my percentage goes down when that happens.

blocks.label: on facing Fils
blocks.text: Arthur for me personally is a very difficult opponent as well because of how much power he has.

blocks.label: on his possible semifinal opponents Medvedev or Tiafoe
blocks.text: Both very, very dangerous opponents and very good tennis players.

blocks.text: I'm happy with the direction my tennis is going in. I want to be the aggressive player.

blocks.label: after his win over Jodar
blocks.text: I knew it wasn't going to be an easy match going in. I was happy that I was able to get through some tough moments in the first set, early when I was down break points, to be able to hold serve and get to that tiebreaker. Once I was in the tiebreaker I felt confident, fending off those set points and coming through it in the end. It was a tricky second set as well, being up a break and losing it, but I thought I fought well, competed well.

blocks.label: on Jodar reaching Turin in his rookie year
blocks.text: Rafa is one of the best young talents that tennis has seen in a long time. To be here playing in Turin in his first year on tour, starting the year outside of top 100, is a ridiculous feat. So I hope all you guys recognize how special that is.

blocks.label: on his semi-final hopes and Fritz vs Zverev
blocks.text: I'm looking forward to it either way. I think both those guys are great guys. I'd love to make the semi-finals here for the first time. I did my job today and, yeah, let's see what happens. I'm always rooting for him. I think him and Sasha are going to have a great match. I think if he takes Sasha out in straights, he gets through to the semi-finals.

blocks.label: on his aggressive game and improved baseline play
blocks.text: I'm trying to be smart in the decisions I make. I still play very aggressively. I pay attention above all to my footwork and I try to take the ball early. I think that when I manage to win the long rallies and come out of them without making wrong decisions or committing unforced errors, that's where opponents struggle the most against me. When I step on court, everyone knows I have a big serve. But if opponents think: OK, I just have to get a few balls back in play and then Ben will miss, it becomes much easier for them to take control and feel comfortable in the rally. When instead the opponent feels he has to do something special to beat me, with the way I'm able to move and cover the court now, which is much better than before, it becomes harder for him to find solutions. So I try to stay true to my identity, play aggressively and come to the net when I can, all this without falling apart from the baseline.

blocks.label: on adapting to the ATP Finals and his return
blocks.text: It's not a tournament where you arrive and immediately feel at ease. This year I changed my mindset on the return.

blocks.label: on his season
blocks.text: Either way, it's been an incredible year for me. I'm happy with the way I competed throughout the year, the way I've bounced back after difficult things have happened, and to win two matches here after making a deep run in Paris as well, I feel that I put a positive end to my season.

latest.text: It’s an important part of our relationship to be able to relate to each other through the different things we go through. Whether it’s media stuff, brand stuff, photoshoots, the pressures of competition and being professional athletes, it is very taxing, … Some people can say that it’s difficult to maintain a relationship where you have two professional athletes. But in my opinion, to have somebody who understands what you go through is very, very important.
